Construction of the bridge was 1357-1402. It was in the late gothic a feat of the engineering. The statues were added later, in Baroque. The towers at the end were part of the active fortification, and helped repelling Swedish army in 1648 (the bridge was the only one over the river at the time).

There are several stories about the bridge, for example a statue of the Turk is told to wander off one night in the year, and chasing women in the streets, looking for a wife. Another one is that the legendary magical sword of the king Bruzwig (not a real king, think Arthur) is buried among the stones. Popular story is about King Wenceslav IV who was imprisoned by the local noblemen. Beautiful barber woman Zuzana helped him escape by providing clothes and boat. The incident is said to inspire kingfisher statues (kingfishers are a symbol of barbers) on the bridge gate. The person to find five kingfishers marks an honest persons.
